sn15.13:1.2: Pāvā, a town of the Mallas, was where Mahāvīra died, plunging the Jains into chaos. (The Jains, however, say this was another Pāvā, east of Nāḷandā.) Perhaps because of this, Pāvā became associated with especially ascetic monks such as those in this discourse: Mahākassapa heard the news of the Buddha’s passing at Pāvā; and monks from Pāvā allied with monks of “Avanti and the south” arguing for strict Vinaya in the Second Council ([pli-tv-kd1:1.7.11]()).
sn15.13:3.12: I can’t help feeling that something stronger is required here for paradarika, i.e rape. But I can’t find any contexts that clarify whether consent was an issue in this crime.
